text:
maria.sales: Customer (NorthBank) requires Canada-only residency for a 3-week POC. They specifically said: no request-level logs or metadata may leave Canada. Can engineering confirm feasibility and a short cost delta? Need answer before tomorrow morning call.
maria.sales: Short please — customer execs will be on the line.

devin.presales: Quick clarifiers: 1) BYOK mandatory or preferred? 2) Will they accept redacted or aggregated telemetry exported out of CA? 3) Any regulatory language we need to echo in an attestation?

maria.sales: BYOK preferred but not hard. They explicitly rejected any raw request-level telemetry leaving CA; aggregated metrics might be okay if non-identifying. They asked for a sub-processor statement.

anya.infra: Current state: our hosted inference region for Canada is ca-central1 for payloads, but some control-plane services (billing, global telemetry aggregator) route to us-east. Options:
- Fast: soft_pin + telemetry redaction config (we keep payloads in CA, redact request IDs before export). ETA: ~48-72 hours for POC config.
- Strong: create dedicated CA reserved pool + regional control-plane routing + regional KMS (BYOK supported). ETA: ~10 days to provision and validate.
- Strict: Private (customer VPC) deploy — full residency and control, ETA varies (weeks).

anya.infra: Caveats: support sessions and remote debug tunnels currently route via support-east; that must be handled with either ephemeral consent or regional control-plane. Also alerting/health signals: we can push summary-level alerts to global pager but keep raw traces in CA.

liam.legal: We can produce a CA-only sub-processor attestation for the dedicated or private options. For the soft_pin (redaction) we'll provide a risk statement and the specific telemetry redaction config but it will not legally guarantee zero-crossing. If NorthBank needs a contractual guarantee, we must scope dedicated pool or private. I'll prepare an attestation template and a short addendum indicating which control-plane components remain region-scoped.

devin.presales: Pricing (rough for a 3-week POC):
- Soft_pin + telemetry config: no change to token pricing, small ops fee ($750) for configuration and verification.
- Dedicated CA reserved (hard_pin) for POC: ~35% uplift on hourly reserved rates + one-time KMS integration fee (~$9k). Minimum booking: 1 week reserve. For 3 weeks expect a temporary uplift estimate (will provide numbers after sizing).
- Private: enterprise quote; not feasible for a short POC.

anya.infra: Example POC routing config we can deploy quickly (submit as JSON policy in the POC request):

"tenant_policy: prefer_region=ca-central1; failover=none; pin_mode=hard; kms=customer_managed; telemetry=redact_request_ids,retain_24h,export_summary_only"

anya.infra: Note: pin_mode=hard enforces tenancy to reserved pool and requires capacity commit. failover=none will return errors if capacity exhausted (safer for residency guarantees).

liam.legal: Action items: I'll draft the attestation + addendum and prepare suggested language for the security questionnaire (BYOK flow, telemetry, access controls).

devin.presales: Action items: I'll model cost estimate after we get QPS and avg seq length from NorthBank (ask for sample traffic profile).

maria.sales: I'll request QPS/profile and confirm whether aggregated metrics are acceptable. Meeting tomorrow 8:30am PT. Please keep replies short so I can forward.

alert-bot: Reminder set for 2 hours before meeting (will ping thread).
